_note: This is an experimental, non-standard static discovery document for cadclaw.io, not an MCP server descriptor or a claim of protocol authority. It lists the read-only resources actually published by https://cadclaw.io. The CADCLAW project separately ships a local MCP server in the `cadclaw_mcp` Python package; it is not hosted at this domain and is listed under `related_packages`, not as a callable site resource.
name: cadclaw.io
description: CADCLAW: automated assembly and validation for STEP-based CAD. Places authored parts by declared constraints, compiles the assembly, then runs geometric, structural, tolerance, and BOM-vs-CAD gates. Static documentation/marketing site for the open-source `cadclaw` Python package.

resources.name: GetPackageInfo
resources.description: CADCLAW home page. HTML with embedded SoftwareApplication + Organization JSON-LD describing the package, version, license, repository, and PyPI download URL.

resources.name: GetLLMsSummary
resources.description: High-density plain-text site summary intended for LLM / agent retrieval (llms.txt convention).

resources.name: GetSitemap
resources.description: XML sitemap listing all crawlable URLs on cadclaw.io.

resources.name: GetRobotsPolicy
resources.description: robots.txt with one global crawler group, explicit Content-Signal policy, and a /cdn-cgi/ exclusion.

related_packages.name: cadclaw
related_packages.description: The CADCLAW Python package itself. Installs the assembly compiler, the validation harness, the `cadclaw` CLI, and the local MCP server.

related_packages.name: cadclaw_mcp
related_packages.description: Local Model Context Protocol server exposing 24 CADCLAW assembly, check, analysis, audit, and render tools, including a stateless versioned run_harness tool and six assemble_* tools that can write configured outputs. Render-producing tools can return PNGs inline and write files. It runs with the local process account's filesystem permissions; it is not a security sandbox and is not hosted at cadclaw.io. Review tool inputs/outputs and use a least-privilege working copy.

auth.note: All listed resources are publicly readable static files.
